entry.title: Pillow fades a P3 photo, sharp clips it: picking the JPEG default per target
entry.summary: The same Display P3 image went through Pillow 11.3 and sharp 0.34.5 with no color options set, and the two JPEGs went wrong in opposite directions. Pillow's copy came out washed out. sharp's copy was right for everyday colors and quietly flattened the most saturated ones. Neither library has a bug here. Each one simply defaults to a different target, and an image pipeline inherits that target unless somebody picks one on purpose. The test material was two HEIC files made with macOS sips, not iPhone originals: a synthetic chart with 12 color patches, and a CC0 photo from Wikimedia Commons converted into Display P3. Both embed a 536-byte P3 profile. Everything ran once on an Apple M4 Mac, both libraries encoded JPEG at quality 90, color difference is CIEDE2000, and sizes are plain bytes. Nei…

entry.title: Business automation agents: separate roles, clear handoffs, owner review
entry.summary: An inbox agent might sort requests and draft replies. A reporting agent prepares summaries from approved sources. A follow-up agent tracks outstanding requests. A coordinator handles dependencies and brings decisions back to the owner; it cannot approve restricted actions itself. The engineering work is in the boundaries: what data each agent can read, what output it must produce, where it hands off and when it must stop for review. I start with a single workflow, test sample work and check failure cases before connecting more systems. My background combines 25+ years of customer-facing technical support with full-stack development, cybersecurity and custom language models. HeshBot, my self-hosted website chatbot, is one example of that work, not a claim that every business integration is already available. AI can make mistakes. Emails, public posts, spending and deletion need explicit owner approval. A useful workflow should be easy to inspect and pause. Read the page: https://trevorheshka.com/ai-agents-business-automation/ https://www.linkedin.com/in/trevorheshka/

entry.summary: Why do some HEIC-to-JPEG conversions come out washed out? The measurements I ran on 2026-11-06 pointed to three checks rather than to a library. Is there an ICC profile after decode, does the encoder carry it or convert the pixels, and what does your inspector actually read. The third is the easiest to get wrong. Scope first.
